chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abu Walad al-Hannat, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah عليه السلام about a woman whose husband had been absent, then returned while she was in i'tikaf with her husband's permission. When news of his arrival reached her, she left the mosque in which she was and prepared herself for her husband until he had intimacy with her.
He عليه السلام said: If she left the mosque before three days had passed, and she had not made a stipulation in her i'tikaf, then upon her is what is upon the muzahir.

key_terms.بِإِذْنِ: With permission; here, with the husband's permission to enter i'tikaf.
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ: Three days, the threshold referenced for this ruling.
key_terms.مُعْتَكِفَةٌ: A woman observing i'tikaf, a spiritual retreat in the mosque.
key_terms.ٱشْتَرَطَتْ: She stipulated a condition beforehand regarding her i'tikaf.
key_terms.ٱعْتِكَافِهَا: Her i'tikaf, the devotional retreat under discussion.
key_terms.ٱلْمَسْجِدِ: The mosque in which the i'tikaf was being observed.
key_terms.ٱلْمُظَاهِرِ: The one who performs zihar; used here as the measure of expiatory liability.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman leaves i'tikaf early for her husband and has marital relations?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning a woman in i'tikaf who leaves before completing three days and then resumes marital relations. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام states that if she had not made a prior stipulation in her i'tikaf, she bears the expiation associated with zihar-like liability mentioned here as that of the muzahir.
